 Craig Ervine Double-Century Secures Draw for Zimbabwe Against Afghanistan
 Zimbabwe's Craig Ervine and Antum Naqvi ©ACB/CW 
 By Cricket World Staff 
 Monday 9 November 2026 
 Afghanistan vs Zimbabwe in UAE 
 Test series Schedule 1st Test, Sharjah Thu 5 Nov Afghanistan 514 169.4 ov Zimbabwe 504 & 523/5 Match Drawn
 Scorecard Stats 
 Craig Ervine produced an unbeaten double-century as Zimbabwe batted through the final day to secure a draw against Afghanistan in the opening Test in Sharjah.
 Match Analysis
 Craig Ervine finished unbeaten on 206 from 279 balls, striking 22 fours and two sixes during a commanding innings that removed any realistic prospect of an Afghanistan victory.
 The result leaves the two-match Afghanistan vs Zimbabwe Test series level ahead of the second and final match.
 Zimbabwe build imposing first-innings total
 Zimbabwe elected to bat and compiled 504 in their first innings, with Brendan Taylor and Brian Bennett both recording centuries.
 Taylor struck 131 from 168 balls, including 14 fours and four sixes, as Zimbabwe reached 326 for five by the close of the opening day .
 Bennett resumed on 71 and progressed to 128 from 206 deliveries. Wesley Madhevere added 54, while Tafadzwa Tsiga made 44 and Graeme Cremer contributed an unbeaten 34.
 Mohammad Saleem Safi and Qais Ahmad claimed three wickets apiece for Afghanistan, while Zia ur Rehman Akbar collected two.
 Afghanistan reply with 514
 Afghanistan produced an equally determined batting performance and secured a narrow 10-run first-innings lead by reaching 514 in 169.4 overs.
 Rahmanullah Zadran and Sediqullah Atal both scored centuries during a substantial second-wicket partnership. Zadran made 102, while Atal contributed 102 before Zimbabwe fought back with a series of wickets.
 Rahmat Shah then anchored the remainder of the innings, scoring 173 as Afghanistan moved beyond Zimbabwe’s first-innings total on the fourth day.
 Afghanistan’s progress beyond 500 and Rahmat’s pivotal innings were central to the fourth day’s play in Sharjah .
 Ervine dominates final day
 Zimbabwe began their second innings late on the fourth day and reached 120 for two before Brendan Taylor was dismissed with the first delivery of day five.
 Brian Bennett made 50 before Ervine assumed control of the innings. The experienced left-hander brought up his half-century from 87 balls and completed his century from 161 deliveries.
 Ervine continued to increase the scoring rate after tea, reaching 150 from 215 balls before completing his double-century from 275 deliveries.
 Antum Naqvi provided valuable support with a half-century, while Madhevere struck 100 from 108 balls. His partnership with Ervine ensured Zimbabwe remained firmly in control throughout the closing stages.
 Ervine finished unbeaten on 206 from 279 balls as the teams agreed to a draw following a Test dominated by six individual centuries and more than 1,500 runs.
 Afghanistan and Zimbabwe will meet again in the second Test in Sharjah, beginning on 13 November.
